units.text: Pick a die. Higher number wins. Whatever you choose, I can pick one with better odds.
units.phonemes: pˈɪk ɐ dˈaɪ. hˈaɪɚ nˈʌmbɚ wˈɪnz. wʌtˈɛvɚ juː tʃˈuːz, aɪ kæn pˈɪk wˈʌn wɪð bˈɛɾɚɹ ˈɑːdz.

units.text: Every face has an equal chance in this puzzle, and neither roll affects the other.
units.phonemes: ˈɛvɹi fˈeɪs hɐz ɐn ˈiːkwəl tʃˈæns ɪn ðɪs pˈʌzəl, ænd nˈiːðɚ ɹˈoʊl ɐfˈɛkts ðɪ ˈʌðɚ.
units.interpretation: Input phonemes are inspectable pronunciation evidence, not subjective listening.

units.text: Yellow always rolls three. Orange has four twos and two sixes. Yellow wins against four faces out of six: two-thirds.
units.phonemes: jˈɛloʊ ˈɔːlweɪz ɹˈoʊlz θɹˈiː. ˈɔɹɪndʒ hɐz fˈoːɹ tˈuːz ænd tˈuː sˈɪksᵻz. jˈɛloʊ wˈɪnz ɐɡˈɛnst fˈoːɹ fˈeɪsᵻz ˌaʊɾəv sˈɪks: tˈuːθˈɜːdz.

units.text: But blue has four fours, so it has better odds against yellow.
units.phonemes: bˌʌt blˈuː hɐz fˈoːɹ fˈoːɹz, sˌoʊ ɪt hɐz bˈɛɾɚɹ ˈɑːdz ɐɡˈɛnst jˈɛloʊ.
units.interpretation: Input phonemes are inspectable pronunciation evidence, not subjective listening.

units.text: Switch to blue? Green’s fives beat every blue face. Its ones still beat blue’s zeros.

units.text: Then orange counters green: its sixes beat everything, and its twos beat green’s ones.

units.text: Every reply shown has those same two-thirds odds. That’s an advantage, not a guaranteed win.

units.text: The advantages form a circle. There’s no best die in this set—just a better matchup.
